patch_description: Add a short-horizon versus full-window slope-consistency gate to the adaptive tracker. The current Kalman correction can respond strongly to a locally noisy innovation even when the recent direction disagrees with the broader trend, contributing to its relatively high slope-change and false-reversal counts. The new statistic computes inexpensive least-squares slopes over the retained measurement window and its newest 6–10 samples. Process noise and measurement gain are restricted when the slopes disagree or have substantially incompatible magnitudes. Coherent sustained motion still retains the normal high-gain response, while isolated turns are smoothed until they gain multi-sample support. This directly trades a small amount of impulsive responsiveness for improved smoothness and reversal reliability without adding phase delay or changing the public API.
